summary: Umatilla NF lookout: a 1925 tree platform, a 1933 96-foot Aermotor tower, a 1966 cabin fire, and a converted shed rented on Recreation.gov today.

facts.design: 96-foot steel Aermotor tower with steel cab, replacing a 1925 tree platform

access.note: Cabin rented through Recreation.gov (combination lock, sent with the reservation). Tower may be climbed only when it is staffed.

visit.trail_note: Tower visitors are welcome to climb only when it is staffed. Over 26 miles of hiking and horse trails can be reached from the cabin. Not open in winter.

facts.agency: US Forest Service, Umatilla National Forest

events.note: Army vocational trainee Frank Bloss took up the lookout post (July 1921 item); on one Tuesday in August 1921 he reported thirteen fires
Platform built in a tree as the first fire lookout on the site
Heppner newspaper item reports a new cabin erected for the lookout; NHLR dates the cabin to 1934
96-foot steel Aermotor tower with steel cab replaces the 1925 tree platform
Cabin for Forest Service personnel (NHLR date)
George Gillis, of the Lexington school faculty, had the summer lookout job (Aug 15, 1935 item)
Lightning strike knocked keeper Max Buschke unconscious for an hour; his wife kept working and reported five fires
Accidental fire destroyed the living quarters cabin; garage/utility shed converted into the current cabin. Tower not affected.
Friends of Blue Mountain Lookouts completed a stair replacement project in September 2021

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources agree on a 96-foot tower (NHLR, Recreation.gov, firelookout.com, and a 1933 newspaper summary). A June 1933 newspaper said a hundred feet and an August 1935 item said 102 feet to the top, likely counting the cab or base differently. The record uses 96 feet.

NHLR dates the cabin to 1934 and Recreation.gov says a neighboring cabin was built alongside the 1933 tower. A January 1931 newspaper item already reports a new cabin erected for the lookout. The story reports both dates and does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: Tower facts agree across four sources; the 1925 and 1933 dates are solid. Cabin date conflicts (1931 newspaper vs 1934 NHLR; firelookout.com says a ground house in 1933). The Heppner newspaper items come from a transcription on oregonlookouts.weebly.com; check the originals (Heppner Gazette-Times) before printing exact wording. The 1966 event is the cabin, not the tower. No drive-up or trailhead directions were found in the sources read, so none are recorded. No photos were recorded. Staffing date is undated on the NHLR page. Recreation.gov notes the cabin's combination is sent with the reservation confirmation, so no combination is recorded.
